newsitem.title: NORWAY: Ailing, freed Kenyan dissident comes to Norway.
newsitem.headline: Ailing, freed Kenyan dissident comes to Norway.

text.p: Ailing Kenyan dissident Koigi wa Wamwere, freed on bail to seek medical treatment, arrived in Norway on Friday but said he would return to Kenya to seek acquittal once he is well.

Wamwere, jailed for four years for robbery in his home country, was greeted at Oslo international airport by his wife Jane and their three sons, including three-year-old Charles whom he has never seen before, Norwegian news agency NTB reported.
"I cannot describe my feelings at this meeting," Wamwere, back in the country where he lived in exile between 1986 and 1990, was quoted as saying by NTB.

Kenyan Chief Justice Abdul Majid Cockar a week ago said he granted Wamwere's temporary liberty on medical and humanitarian grounds, but said he hoped the dissident would return to Kenya after undergoing treatment to face the appeal he has lodged.

Wamwere was admitted to the private Nairobi Hospital last month with cardiac complications. Kenyan cardiologists say he requires surgery to live, and he is expected to undergo treatment in Oslo and in London.
Wamwere, who was exiled in Norway between 1986 and 1990, said he would go back to Kenya although his wife and children still live in Norway.

"Norway is my second homeland," he said. "I want to stay here and I don't want to stay here. But if I don't go back to the trial, everyone will think that I was guilty and that I ran away to escape punishment. But I am innocent, and I shall prove it," he told reporters.

Wamwere and two others -- including his brother Charles -- were jailed for four years in October 1995 for robbery. A fourth man was freed for lack of clear evidence. They have appealed against the sentence, arguing that the magistrate erred in law.
The London-based human rights group Amnesty International has adopted Wamwere as a prisoner of conscience, saying that Kenyan authorities were punishing him for his political beliefs.

Wamwere is a former member of parliament for a constituency that includes President Daniel arap Moi's rural Kabarak home in his native Rift Valley province. Norway has condemned Wamwere's conviction as a travesty of the justice.
